answer_text:
Take the group of square roots of \(1\) in the multiplicative group over \(\mathbb C\):

\[
G=\mu_2=\{x\in \mathbb G_m \mid x^2=1\}
=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[t]/(t^2-1).
\]

Step by step:

1. \(\mathbb G_m=\operatorname{GL}_1\) is a linear algebraic group.
2. The condition \(x^2=1\) defines a closed subgroup of \(\mathbb G_m\), so \(\mu_2\) is a linear algebraic group.
3. Its \(\mathbb C\)-rational points are
   \[
   G(\mathbb C)=\{x\in \mathbb C^\times : x^2=1\}=\{1,-1\}.
   \]
   These are exactly two points.

Thus an example is

\[
\boxed{G=\mu_2=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[t]/(t^2-1)\subset \mathbb G_m}
\]

which has exactly two \(\mathbb C\)-rational points.
